  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4

```{r setup}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

Beta diversity measures how communities differ. Baselga (2010) showed that
dissimilarity has two parts: **turnover**, where species replace each
other, and **nestedness**, where poorer sites hold a subset of the species
at richer sites. The examples use `ant_gradient`, a simulated dataset.

## Pairwise dissimilarity

```{r}
pairs <- beta_pair(ant_gradient, .by = transect)
pairs
```

Turnover and nestedness add up to the total. Use `index = "jaccard"` for
the Jaccard family. The results match the betapart package.

```{r}
pairs |>
  group_by(transect) |>
  summarise(across(c(turnover, nestedness, total), mean))
```

## Many sites at once

```{r}
beta_multi(ant_gradient, .by = transect)
```

## Distance decay

`beta_decay()` adds the distance between sites along a gradient. Here
turnover rises with elevational distance while nestedness stays low.

```{r}
decay <- beta_decay(ant_gradient, gradient = elevation, .by = transect)
decay
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Dissimilarity against elevational distance"}
autoplot(decay)
```
